title: AI Medical Interpretation for Patient Navigators
summary: Define navigator, CHW, and interpreter roles. Learn how to use AI medical interpretation, escalation rules, documentation, and pilot metrics.
body_markdown:
###


Start with Opalite Health for most navigation visits after confirming the patient's preferred language and dialect, testing connectivity, and completing your pre-session checklist. Choose qualified bilingual staff within assessed scope or a phone or video interpreter when a dialect mismatch occurs, the patient requests a different option, or your pilot data shows unresolved communication concerns for that language. Base the decision on your organization's approved language-access policy, not on the perceived complexity of the visit.


###


Pause the conversation, name the uncertainty out loud to the patient, and follow your organization's escalation steps before continuing. Community health workers and patient navigators can flag a problem but cannot verify meaning in a language they don't know, so reconnect through your designated backup or involve the responsible clinician. Never guess at missing meaning; requesting help is part of the protocol, not a failure.


###


Bilingual ability does not qualify staff to interpret, so the two are not interchangeable. Opalite Health handles approved interpretation tasks, freeing community health workers and patient navigators for navigation work such as referral coordination, transportation, and follow-up. Where a staff member holds separate assessed interpreter qualifications, your responsibility matrix should define that role explicitly and require a role-change announcement to the patient.


###


Track connection time, completed referrals, unresolved language requests, and patient-reported understanding, then segment every result by language, dialect, setting, and interpretation method. Aggregate numbers can hide gaps; a pilot that performs well for Spanish speakers may still leave Somali-speaking patients without resolved communication. Pair cost per supported encounter with quality indicators and escalation counts before deciding whether to expand to another clinic or language group.


###


A dedicated phone workflow may work without requiring the patient to use a smartphone or internet connection, but you must confirm your Opalite Health deployment supports the specific call setup and test it from the patient's side before scheduling outreach. Assign navigators a backup contact method and a clear reconnection process for interrupted calls. Check your vendor agreement for data-handling and retention settings that apply to phone-based sessions.


###


Integrated care depends on consistent communication across referrals, follow-up, and care transitions. Approved AI interpretation from Opalite Health keeps that communication consistent when you pair it with pause and escalation rules. Community health workers and patient navigators stay responsible for coordinating referrals, follow-up, and handoffs. They do not verify interpretation accuracy.
